key_insight: Neural networks can learn to predict ground-state observables of a 2D interacting quantum system from experimental quantum-generated data, even for unseen Hamiltonian settings.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable route for using quantum processors as data sources to estimate many-body properties beyond the reach of classical simulation.
method: Generated experimental datasets from approximate ground states of the 2D Heisenberg XXZ model up to 115 qubits.
Collected single-site expectation values, two-point correlations, and 12-body loop correlations across the antiferromagnetic phase.
Trained neural networks to predict spatially resolved observables for unseen Hamiltonian parameters.
evidence_signal: The models accurately predicted observables both within the training distribution and in an out-of-distribution regime near the phase boundary using data from up to 115-qubit experiments.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of approximate ground-state preparation, so noise, finite-size effects, and phase-boundary generalization remain practical concerns.
paper_title: Learning ground state observables from quantum computing experiments
